Repacked a single-primitive GLB, then ran glTF-Transform weld -> simplify (ratio 0.28, error 0.01) -> quantize (KHR_mesh_quantization) to go from 1,900,050 to 50,407 triangles and from 66.9 MB to 1.42 MB while preserving the flat playing surface's texture and markings

operations: Fetched the public Terrarium z10 elevation tile (about 150 m/pixel at this latitude) covering 11.3299 N, 142.1993 E with scripts/build_dem_block.py --mode sea; z11/z12 tiles in this remote area returned flat, no-data pixels and were not usable

Built an opaque seafloor top surface colored by a depth-stretched bathymetric ramp, plus opaque rock walls dropping from the terrain boundary to a flat base 300 m below the deepest point and a floor cap closing the block

Added a second, translucent primitive (alphaMode BLEND, RGBA vertex colors) for the water shell: a flat quad at sea level (y=0) plus walls following the terrain boundary from y=0 down to the seafloor, colored lighter/more transparent near the top and darker/more opaque toward the bottom
Packed both primitives into one GLB buffer (scripts/fetch_model_assets.py pack_glb); no Draco, meshopt, or external textures

models.note: PDB 1KX5 nucleosome core particle: both 147-base DNA strands and all eight histones, including resolved histone tails. DNA is amber; histones are colored by chain. The approximate 11 nm value describes the DNA-wrapped disc; resolved tails extend beyond it. Unresolved residues, water and ions are omitted.

models.name: Tobacco Mosaic Virus
models.author: Namba, K., Pattanayek, R., Stubbs, G.
models.note: A 300 nm-long flat-cut lattice reconstruction from PDB 2TMV protein and RNA coordinates and its deposited helical symmetry. The coat is teal and the RNA amber. The central channel and repeating surface follow the structural coordinates. This representative rod length uses repeated structural subunits; the two end planes are authored cuts, not experimentally reconstructed virion ends. The smooth display surface does not resolve individual atoms.

models.name: Ribosome
models.author: Ben-Shem, A., Garreau de Loubresse, N., Melnikov, S., Jenner, L., Yusupova, G., Yusupov, M.
models.note: Author-defined biological assembly 1 of PDB 4V88: one yeast 80S ribosome, not the two particles in the asymmetric unit. Ribosomal RNA is gold; protein chains use a contrasting palette. Includes the deposited Stm1 protein; unmodeled residues, water and ions are omitted. Native coordinates are preserved, independently of the approximate 30 nm catalog value.

models.name: Buckminsterfullerene
models.author: Kim, K.-H., Ko, D.-K., Kim, Y.-T., Kim, N.H., Paul, J., Zhang, S.-Q., Murray, C.B., Acharya, R., DeGrado, W.F., Kim, Y.H., Grigoryan, G.
models.note: Experimental C60 cage from the 60C ligand in PDB 5ET3. The thin atoms and bonds mark nuclear positions, not van der Waals radii; the listed 0.71 nm is a nucleus-to-nucleus cage diameter. The surrounding binding peptide is omitted.

models.name: Actin Filament
models.author: Gurel, P.S., Kim, L.Y., Ruijgrok, P.V., Omabegho, T., Bryant, Z., Alushin, G.M.
models.note: A 7 nm-long, flat-cut window through the experimental rabbit actin lattice of PDB 6BNO. Alternating deposited subunits have contrasting colors. Both ends are visualization cuts, not filament ends. The listed 7 nm is an approximate filament diameter; the irregular structural envelope can be wider. This short window does not show a complete helical crossover.

models.name: Microtubule
models.author: Zhang, R., LaFrance, B., Nogales, E.
models.note: A 20 nm-long, flat-cut window through a reconstructed 14-protofilament GMPCPP microtubule lattice from PDB 6DPU. Alpha tubulin is teal and beta tubulin violet. Neighboring-protofilament and longitudinal transforms are fitted to matching deposited C-alpha coordinates. The seam is inferred; seam-specific conformations and disordered tails are unresolved. The generic 25 nm diameter is approximate; this in-vitro 14-protofilament example is wider than a common 13-protofilament cellular microtubule.

models.name: SARS-CoV-2 Spike
models.author: Walls, A.C., Park, Y.J., Tortorici, M.A., Wall, A., McGuire, A.T., Veesler, D.
models.note: PDB 6VXX closed prefusion spike ectodomain trimer, colored by protein chain, with only deposited glycan residues shown in gold. This engineered soluble construct resolves about 16 nm of the roughly 20 nm membrane-projecting spike; missing flexible stalk, membrane anchor and unresolved glycans are not invented. It is not the whole virus.

models.name: Nuclear Pore Complex
models.author: Mosalaganti, S., Obarska-Kosinska, A., Siggel, M., Taniguchi, R., Turonova, B., Zimmerli, C.E., Buczak, K., Schmidt, F.H., Margiotta, E., Mackmull, M.T., Hagen, W.J.H., Hummer, G., Kosinski, J., Beck, M.
models.note: Full eightfold assembly of PDB 7R5K, a constricted human nuclear pore scaffold modeled integratively using cryo-electron tomography and predicted protein structures. A deliberately coarse C-alpha envelope, colored by nucleoporin entity, preserves the central channel and deposited eightfold transforms. Disordered transport barrier, nuclear membranes and unresolved basket/filaments are absent. It is not an atomically resolved complete pore.
